english_source:
3949 — Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAṭā, the freedman of ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, narrated from his father that Ziyād, or one of the governors, appointed ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn over the charity collection. When he returned, he said to ʿImrān, “Where is the money?” He replied, “Was it for the money that you sent me? We took it from where we used to take it during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we placed it where we used to place it during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1625) and Ibn Mājah (1811).

These hadiths are used as evidence that the zakat of each land should be distributed to its own poor people. However, if it is not possible to identify the poor of that land, then it is permissible to transfer it to the poor of another land, just as the zakat of the desert Arabs used to be brought to Madinah and given to the poor among the Emigrants and the Helpers.

٣٩٥٠ — عن أنس بن مالك، أن أبا بكر رضي الله عنه كتب له هذا الكتاب لما وجَّهه إلى البحرين:

«بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ.

هَذِهِ فَرِيضَةُ الصَّدَقَةِ الَّتِي فَرَضَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ، وَالَّتِي أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا رَسُولَهُ، فَمَنْ سُئِلَهَا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ عَلَى وَجْهِهَا فَلْيُعْطِهَا، وَمَنْ سُئِلَ فَوْقَهَا فَلَا يُعْطِ.

فِي أَرْبَعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ مِنَ الْإِبِلِ فَمَا دُونَهَا مِنَ الْغَنَمِ، مِنْ كُلِّ خَمْسٍ شَاةٌ.

فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ خَمْسًا وَعِشْرِينَ إِلَى خَمْسٍ وَثَلَاثِينَ فَفِيهَا بِنْتُ مَخَاضٍ أُنْثَى.

فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ سِتًّا وَثَلَاثِينَ إِلَى خَمْسٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ فَفِيهَا بِنْتُ لَبُونٍ أُنْثَى.

فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ سِتًّا وَأَرْبَعِينَ إِلَى سِتِّينَ فَفِيهَا حِقَّةٌ طَرُوقَةُ الْجَمَلِ.

فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ وَاحِدَةً وَسِتِّينَ إِلَى خَمْسٍ وَسَبْعِينَ فَفِيهَا جَذَعَةٌ.

فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ يَعْنِي سِتًّا وَسَبْعِينَ إِلَى تِسْعِينَ فَفِيهَا بِنْتَا لَبُونٍ.

فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ إِحْدَى وَتِسْعِينَ إِلَى عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةٍ فَفِيهَا حِقَّتَانِ طَرُوقَتَا الْجَمَلِ.

فَإِذَا زَادَتْ عَلَى عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةٍ، فَفِي كُلِّ أَرْبَعِينَ بِنْتُ لَبُونٍ، وَفِي كُلِّ خَمْسِينَ حِقَّةٌ.

وَمَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ مَعَهُ إِلَّا أَرْبَعٌ مِنَ الْإِبِلِ فَلَيْسَ فِيهَا صَدَقَةٌ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ رَبُّهَا، فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ خَمْسًا مِنَ الْإِبِلِ فَفِيهَا شَاةٌ.

وَفِي صَدَقَةِ الْغَنَمِ فِي سَائِمَتِهَا إِذَا كَانَتْ أَرْبَعِينَ إِلَى عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةٍ شَاةٌ.

فَإِذَا زَادَتْ عَلَى عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةٍ إِلَى مِائَتَيْنِ شَاتَانِ.

فَإِذَا زَادَتْ عَلَى مِائَتَيْنِ إِلَى ثَلَاثِ مِائَةٍ فَفِيهَا ثَلَاثُ شِيَاهٍ.

فَإِذَا زَادَتْ عَلَى ثَلَاثِ مِائَةٍ فَفِي كُلِّ مِائَةٍ شَاةٌ.

فَإِذَا كَانَتْ سَائِمَةُ الرَّجُلِ نَاقِصَةً مِنْ أَرْبَعِينَ شَاةً وَاحِدَةً فَلَيْسَ فِيهَا صَدَقَةٌ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ رَبُّهَا.

وَفِي الرِّقَّةِ رُبْعُ الْعُشْرِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ إِلَّا تِسْعِينَ وَمِائَةً فَلَيْسَ فِيهَا شَيْءٌ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ رَبُّهَا».

صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٤٥٤).

٣٩٥١ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( ليس فيما دون خمس من الإبل صدقة، ولا في الأربع شيء، فإذا بلغت خمسًا ففيها شاة إلى أن تبلغ تسعًا، فإذا بلغت عشرًا ففيها شاتان إلى أن تبلغ أربع عشرة، فإذا بلغت خمس عشرة ففيها ثلاث شياه إلى أن تبلغ تسع عشرة، فإذا بلغت عشرين ففيها أربع شياه إلى أن تبلغ أربعًا وعشرين، فإذا بلغت خمسًا وعشرين ففيها بنت مخاض إلى خمس وثلاثين، فإذا لم تكن بنت مخاض فابن لبون ذكر، فإن زادت بعيرًا ففيها بنت لبون إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وأربعين، فإن زادت بعيرًا ففيها حقة إلى أن تبلغ ستين، فإن زادت بعيرًا ففيها جذعة إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وسبعين، فإن زادت بعيرًا ففيها بنتا لبون إلى أن تبلغ تسعين، فإن زادت بعيرًا ففيها حقتان إلى أن تبلغ عشرين ومائة، ثم في كل خمسين حقة، وفي كل أربعين بنت لبون )).

٣٩٥١ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( ليس فيما دون خمس من الإبل صدقة، ولا في الأربع شيء، فإذا بلغت خمسًا ففيها شاة إلى أن تبلغ تسعًا، فإذا بلغت عشرًا ففيها شاتان إلى أن تبلغ أربع عشرة، فإذا بلغت خمس عشرة ففيها ثلاث شياه إلى أن تبلغ تسع عشرة، فإذا بلغت عشرين ففيها أربع شياه إلى أن تبلغ أربعًا وعشرين، فإذا بلغت خمسًا وعشرين ففيها بنت مخاض إلى خمس وثلاثين، فإذا لم تكن بنت مخاض فابن لبون ذكر، فإن زادت بعيرًا ففيها بنت لبون إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وأربعين، فإن زادت بعيرًا ففيها حقة إلى أن تبلغ ستين، فإن زادت بعيرًا ففيها جذعة إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وسبعين، فإن زادت بعيرًا ففيها بنتا لبون إلى أن تبلغ تسعين، فإن زادت بعيرًا ففيها حقتان إلى أن تبلغ عشرين ومائة، ثم في كل خمسين حقة، وفي كل أربعين بنت لبون )).

3951 — Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “There is no obligatory charity on fewer than five camels. There is nothing due on four. Once they reach five, then one sheep is due until they reach nine. Once they reach ten, then two sheep are due until they reach fourteen. Once they reach fifteen, then three sheep are due until they reach nineteen. Once they reach twenty, then four sheep are due until they reach twenty-four. Once they reach twenty-five, then one she-camel in her second year is due until they reach thirty-five. If such a camel is not available, then a male camel in its third year is due. If there is one more camel, then one she-camel in her third year is due until they reach forty-five. If there is one more camel, then one she-camel in her fourth year is due until they reach sixty. If there is one more camel, then one she-camel in her fifth year is due until they reach seventy-five. If there is one more camel, then two she-camels in their third year are due until they reach ninety. If there is one more camel, then two she-camels in their fourth year are due until they reach one hundred and twenty. After that, for every fifty there is one she-camel in her fourth year due, and for every forty there is one she-camel in her third year due.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ibn Majah (1799).

arabic_source:
٣٩٥٣ — عن قزعة بن يحيى البصري قال:

أتيت أبا سعيد وهو مكثور عليه، فلما تفرق الناس عنه قلت:

إني لا أسألك عما يسألك هؤلاء عنه، أسألك عن صلاة رسول الله ﷺ.

فقال:

ما لك في ذلك من خير.

فأعادها عليه، فقال:

كانت صلاة الظهر تقام، فينطلق أحدنا إلى البقيع فيقضي حاجته، ثم يأتي أهله فيتوضأ، ثم يرجع إلى المسجد ورسول الله ﷺ في الركعة الأولى.

قال:

وسألته عن الزكاة، فقال:

لا أدري أرفعه إلى النبي ﷺ أم لا:

«فِي مِائَتَيْ دِرْهَمٍ خَمْسَةُ دَرَاهِمَ، وَفِي أَرْبَعِينَ شَاةً شَاةٌ إِلَى عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةٍ، فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا شَاتَانِ إِلَى مِائَتَيْنِ، فَإِذَا زَادَتْ فَفِيهَا ثَلَاثُ شِيَاهٍ إِلَى ثَلَاثِ مِائَةٍ، فَإِذَا زَادَتْ فَفِي كُلِّ مِائَةٍ شَاةٌ.

وَفِي الْإِبِلِ: فِي خَمْسٍ شَاةٌ، وَفِي عَشْرٍ شَاتَانِ، وَفِي خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ ثَلَاثُ شِيَاهٍ، وَفِي عِشْرِينَ أَرْبَعُ شِيَاهٍ، وَفِي خَمْسٍ وَعِشْرِينَ ابْنَةُ مَخَاضٍ إِلَى خَمْسٍ وَثَلَاثِينَ.

فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا ابْنَةُ لَبُونٍ إِلَى خَمْسٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ.

فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا حِقَّةٌ إِلَى سِتِّينَ.

فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا جَذَعَةٌ إِلَى خَمْسٍ وَسَبْعِينَ.

فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا ابْنَتَا لَبُونٍ إِلَى تِسْعِينَ.

فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا حِقَّتَانِ إِلَى عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةٍ.

فَإِذَا زَادَتْ فَفِي كُلِّ خَمْسِينَ حِقَّةٌ، وَفِي كُلِّ أَرْبَعِينَ بِنْتُ لَبُونٍ».

وسألته عن الصوم في السفر، فقال:

سافرنا مع رسول الله ﷺ إلى مكة ونحن صيام، فنزلنا منزلًا، فقال رسول الله ﷺ:

3953 — Qazaʿah ibn Yaḥyā al-Baṣrī said:

I came to Abū Saʿīd while many people were gathered around him. When the people dispersed, I said:

“I am not going to ask you about what these people were asking you. I want to ask you about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”

He said:

“There is no good for you in asking about that.”

I repeated the question, so he said:

“The Ẓuhr prayer would be established, and one of us would go to al-Baqīʿ to relieve himself, then return to his family and perform wuḍūʾ, then return to the mosque while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was still in the first rakʿah.”

He said:

I asked him about zakat, and he replied:

“I do not know whether he attributed this to the Prophet ﷺ or not:

On two hundred dirhams, five dirhams are due.

On forty sheep, one sheep is due up to one hundred and twenty. If they increase by one, two sheep are due up to two hundred. If they increase beyond that, three sheep are due up to three hundred. If they increase beyond three hundred, one sheep is due for every hundred.

Regarding camels: for five camels, one sheep is due; for ten, two sheep; for fifteen, three sheep; for twenty, four sheep; and for twenty-five, one bint makhāḍ is due up to thirty-five.

If they increase by one, one bint labūn is due up to forty-five.

If they increase by one, one ḥiqqah is due up to sixty.

If they increase by one, one jadhaʿah is due up to seventy-five.

If they increase by one, two bint labūn camels are due up to ninety.

If they increase by one, two ḥiqqah camels are due up to one hundred and twenty.

If they exceed that, then for every fifty one ḥiqqah is due, and for every forty one bint labūn is due.”

I also asked him about fasting while traveling. He said:

“We traveled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ toward Makkah while we were fasting. We stopped at a place, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

‘You have drawn near to your enemy, and breaking the fast will make you stronger.’

So it was a concession. Some of us fasted and some broke their fast.

Then we stopped at another place, and he said:

‘You will meet your enemy in the morning, and breaking the fast will make you stronger, so break your fast.’

This time it was a firm command, so we broke our fast.

Afterward, I saw us fasting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while traveling.”

Authentic: Narrated in full by Aḥmad (11307); Muslim (1120) narrates the fasting portion in abbreviated form.

If they increase by one, two bint labūn camels are due up to ninety.

If they increase by one, two ḥiqqah camels are due up to one hundred and twenty.

3954 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar reported:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote a document concerning zakat, but he died before sending it to his officials. He kept it attached to his sword. Abū Bakr acted according to it until he died, then ʿUmar acted according to it until he died. It contained:

“For five camels, one sheep is due; for ten, two sheep; for fifteen, three sheep; and for twenty, four sheep.

For twenty-five up to thirty-five camels, one female bint makhāḍ is due. If they increase by one, then one bint labūn is due up to forty-five. If they increase by one, then one ḥiqqah is due up to sixty. If they increase by one, then one jadhaʿah is due up to seventy-five. If they increase by one, then two bint labūn camels are due up to ninety. If they increase by one, then two ḥiqqah camels are due up to one hundred and twenty.

If the camels exceed that, then for every fifty one ḥiqqah is due, and for every forty one bint labūn is due.

Regarding sheep: for every forty sheep, one sheep is due up to one hundred and twenty. If they increase by one, two sheep are due up to two hundred. If they increase by one beyond two hundred, three sheep are due up to three hundred. If they exceed three hundred, one sheep is due for every hundred. And nothing is due on them until they reach one hundred.

Animals belonging to one combined flock must not be separated, and separate flocks must not be combined, out of fear of zakat. If two owners have mixed property, they must settle between themselves equitably. Neither an old animal nor a defective animal is to be taken as zakat.”

Al-Zuhrī said:

“When the zakat collector comes, the sheep are divided into three groups: the inferior, the superior, and the middle-quality animals. The collector takes from the middle.”

Al-Zuhrī did not mention cattle.

Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1568) and al-Tirmidhī (621).

وَلَا يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَ مُجْتَمِعٍ، وَلَا يُجْمَعُ بَيْنَ مُتَفَرِّقٍ مَخَافَةَ الصَّدَقَةِ، وَمَا كَانَ مِنْ خَلِيطَيْنِ فَإِنَّهُمَا يَتَرَاجَعَانِ بَيْنَهُمَا بِالسَّوِيَّةِ، وَلَا يُؤْخَذُ فِي الصَّدَقَةِ هَرِمَةٌ وَلَا ذَاتُ عَيْبٍ».

وقال الزهري:

إذا جاء المصدق قُسمت الشاء أثلاثًا: ثلثًا شرارًا، وثلثًا خيارًا، وثلثًا وسطًا، فأخذ المصدق من الوسط.

ولم يذكر الزهري البقر.

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٦٨)، والترمذي (٦٢١).

3954 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar reported:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote a document concerning zakat, but he died before sending it to his officials. He kept it attached to his sword. Abū Bakr acted according to it until he died, then ʿUmar acted according to it until he died. It contained:

“For five camels, one sheep is due; for ten, two sheep; for fifteen, three sheep; and for twenty, four sheep.

For twenty-five up to thirty-five camels, one female bint makhāḍ is due. If they increase by one, then one bint labūn is due up to forty-five. If they increase by one, then one ḥiqqah is due up to sixty. If they increase by one, then one jadhaʿah is due up to seventy-five. If they increase by one, then two bint labūn camels are due up to ninety. If they increase by one, then two ḥiqqah camels are due up to one hundred and twenty.

If the camels exceed that, then for every fifty one ḥiqqah is due, and for every forty one bint labūn is due.

Regarding sheep: for every forty sheep, one sheep is due up to one hundred and twenty. If they increase by one, two sheep are due up to two hundred. If they increase by one beyond two hundred, three sheep are due up to three hundred. If they exceed three hundred, one sheep is due for every hundred. And nothing is due on them until they reach one hundred.

Animals belonging to one combined flock must not be separated, and separate flocks must not be combined, out of fear of zakat. If two owners have mixed property, they must settle between themselves equitably. Neither an old animal nor a defective animal is to be taken as zakat.”

Al-Zuhrī said:

“When the zakat collector comes, the sheep are divided into three groups: the inferior, the superior, and the middle-quality animals. The collector takes from the middle.”

Al-Zuhrī did not mention cattle.

Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1568) and al-Tirmidhī (621).

٣٩٥٥ — عن علي رضي الله عنه - قال زهير: أحسبه عن النبي ﷺ - أنه قال:

«هَاتُوا رُبْعَ الْعُشُورِ، مِنْ كُلِّ أَرْبَعِينَ دِرْهَمًا دِرْهَمٌ، وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ شَيْءٌ حَتَّى تَتِمَّ مِائَتَيْ دِرْهَمٍ، فَإِذَا كَانَتْ مِائَتَيْ دِرْهَمٍ فَفِيهَا خَمْسَةُ دَرَاهِمَ، فَمَا زَادَ فَعَلَى حِسَابِ ذَلِكَ.

وَفِي الْغَنَمِ فِي كُلِّ أَرْبَعِينَ شَاةً شَاةٌ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ إِلَّا تِسْعٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ فِيهَا شَيْءٌ».

وساق صدقة الغنم مثل الزهري.

وقال:

«وَفِي الْبَقَرِ فِي كُلِّ ثَلَاثِينَ تَبِيعٌ، وَفِي الْأَرْبَعِينَ مُسِنَّةٌ، وَلَيْسَ عَلَى الْعَوَامِلِ شَيْءٌ».

وفي الإبل ذكر صدقتها كما ذكر الزهري.

وقال: «وَفِي خَمْسٍ وَعِشْرِينَ خَمْسٌ مِنَ الْغَنَمِ، فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا ابْنَةُ مَخَاضٍ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ بِنْتُ مَخَاضٍ فَابْنُ لَبُونٍ ذَكَرٌ إِلَى خَمْسٍ وَثَلَاثِينَ، فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا بِنْتُ لَبُونٍ إِلَى خَمْسٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ، فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا حِقَّةٌ طَرُوقَةُ الْجَمَلِ إِلَى سِتِّينَ».

ثم ساق مثل حديث الزهري.

وقال: «فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً — يَعْنِي وَاحِدَةً وَتِسْعِينَ — فَفِيهَا حِقَّتَانِ طَرُوقَتَا الْجَمَلِ إِلَى عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةٍ، فَإِنْ كَانَتِ الْإِبِلُ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَفِي كُلِّ خَمْسِينَ حِقَّةٌ».

وقال:

«وَلَا يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَ مُجْتَمِعٍ، وَلَا يُجْمَعُ بَيْنَ مُفْتَرِقٍ خَشْيَةَ الصَّدَقَةِ، وَلَا تُؤْخَذُ فِي الصَّدَقَةِ هَرِمَةٌ، وَلَا ذَاتُ عَوَارٍ، وَلَا تَيْسٌ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ الْمُصَدِّقُ.

وَفِي النَّبَاتِ مَا سَقَتْهُ الْأَنْهَارُ أَوْ سَقَتِ السَّمَاءُ الْعُشْرُ، وَمَا سَقَى الْغَرْبُ فَفِيهِ نِصْفُ الْعُشْرِ».

وفي حديث عاصم والحارث:

«الصَّدَقَةُ فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ».

قال زهير: أحسبه قال: «مرة».

وفي حديث عاصم:

«إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِي الْإِبِلِ ابْنَةُ مَخَاضٍ وَلَا ابْنُ لَبُونٍ فَعَشَرَةُ دَرَاهِمَ أَوْ شَاتَانِ».

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٧٢).

3955 — ʿAlī reported—and Zuhayr said, “I think he attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ”—that he said:

“Give one-quarter of one-tenth. For every forty dirhams, one dirham is due. Nothing is due until the amount reaches two hundred dirhams. When it reaches two hundred dirhams, five dirhams are due, and whatever exceeds that is calculated according to the same proportion.

Regarding sheep, one sheep is due for every forty. If there are only thirty-nine, nothing is due.”

He then narrated the zakat regulations concerning sheep in the same manner as al-Zuhrī.

He said:

“Regarding cattle, for every thirty one yearling calf is due, and for every forty one musinnah is due. Nothing is due on working cattle.”

He also mentioned the zakat regulations concerning camels in the same manner as al-Zuhrī.

He said: “For twenty-five camels, five sheep are due. If they increase by one, then one bint makhāḍ is due; and if no bint makhāḍ is available, then a male ibn labūn is due up to thirty-five. If they increase by one, then one bint labūn is due up to forty-five. If they increase by one, then one ḥiqqah fit for breeding is due up to sixty.”

Then he continued with wording like al-Zuhrī’s report.

He said: “If they increase by one — meaning to ninety-one — then two ḥiqqah camels fit for breeding are due up to one hundred and twenty. If the camels exceed that, then for every fifty one ḥiqqah is due.”

He said:

“A combined herd is not to be separated, nor separate herds combined, out of fear of zakat. An old animal, an animal with an obvious defect, or a breeding male goat is not to be taken as zakat unless the collector wishes.

Regarding crops, whatever is irrigated by rivers or rain is subject to one-tenth, while whatever is irrigated by drawing water is subject to one-half of one-tenth.”

In the narration of ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥārith:

“Zakat is due every year.”

Zuhayr said:

“I think he said: once.”

And in ʿĀṣim’s narration:

“If neither a bint makhāḍ nor a male ibn labūn is available among the camels, then ten dirhams or two sheep are due.”

Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1572).

وقال: «فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً — يَعْنِي وَاحِدَةً وَتِسْعِينَ — فَفِيهَا حِقَّتَانِ طَرُوقَتَا الْجَمَلِ إِلَى عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةٍ، فَإِنْ كَانَتِ الْإِبِلُ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَفِي كُلِّ خَمْسِينَ حِقَّةٌ».

وقال:

«وَلَا يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَ مُجْتَمِعٍ، وَلَا يُجْمَعُ بَيْنَ مُفْتَرِقٍ خَشْيَةَ الصَّدَقَةِ، وَلَا تُؤْخَذُ فِي الصَّدَقَةِ هَرِمَةٌ، وَلَا ذَاتُ عَوَارٍ، وَلَا تَيْسٌ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ الْمُصَدِّقُ.

وَفِي النَّبَاتِ مَا سَقَتْهُ الْأَنْهَارُ أَوْ سَقَتِ السَّمَاءُ الْعُشْرُ، وَمَا سَقَى الْغَرْبُ فَفِيهِ نِصْفُ الْعُشْرِ».

وفي حديث عاصم والحارث:

«الصَّدَقَةُ فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ».

قال زهير: أحسبه قال: «مرة».

وفي حديث عاصم:

«إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِي الْإِبِلِ ابْنَةُ مَخَاضٍ وَلَا ابْنُ لَبُونٍ فَعَشَرَةُ دَرَاهِمَ أَوْ شَاتَانِ».

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٧٢).

3955 — ʿAlī reported—and Zuhayr said, “I think he attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ”—that he said:

“Give one-quarter of one-tenth. For every forty dirhams, one dirham is due. Nothing is due until the amount reaches two hundred dirhams. When it reaches two hundred dirhams, five dirhams are due, and whatever exceeds that is calculated according to the same proportion.

Regarding sheep, one sheep is due for every forty. If there are only thirty-nine, nothing is due.”

He then narrated the zakat regulations concerning sheep in the same manner as al-Zuhrī.

He said:

“Regarding cattle, for every thirty one yearling calf is due, and for every forty one musinnah is due. Nothing is due on working cattle.”

He also mentioned the zakat regulations concerning camels in the same manner as al-Zuhrī.

He said: “For twenty-five camels, five sheep are due. If they increase by one, then one bint makhāḍ is due; and if no bint makhāḍ is available, then a male ibn labūn is due up to thirty-five. If they increase by one, then one bint labūn is due up to forty-five. If they increase by one, then one ḥiqqah fit for breeding is due up to sixty.”

Then he continued with wording like al-Zuhrī’s report.

He said: “If they increase by one — meaning to ninety-one — then two ḥiqqah camels fit for breeding are due up to one hundred and twenty. If the camels exceed that, then for every fifty one ḥiqqah is due.”

He said:

“A combined herd is not to be separated, nor separate herds combined, out of fear of zakat. An old animal, an animal with an obvious defect, or a breeding male goat is not to be taken as zakat unless the collector wishes.

Regarding crops, whatever is irrigated by rivers or rain is subject to one-tenth, while whatever is irrigated by drawing water is subject to one-half of one-tenth.”

In the narration of ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥārith:

“Zakat is due every year.”

Zuhayr said:

“I think he said: once.”

And in ʿĀṣim’s narration:

“If neither a bint makhāḍ nor a male ibn labūn is available among the camels, then ten dirhams or two sheep are due.”

Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1572).

٣٩٥٦ — عن أبي بكر بن محمد بن عمرو بن حزم، عن أبيه، عن جدّه: أن رسولَ اللّٰه ﷺ كتب إلى أهل اليمن بكتاب فيه الفرائض والسُّنن والدِّيات، وبعث به مع عمرو بن حزم، فقرئت على أهل اليمن، وهذه نسختها: (( من محمد النبي ﷺ إلى شرحبيل بن عبد كلال، والحارث بن عبد كلال، ونعيم بن عبد كلال، قيل ذي رُعَينٍ ومعافر وهمدان: أمّا بعد، فقد رجع رسولكم، وأعطيتم من الغنائم خُمس اللّٰه، وما كتب اللّٰه على المؤمنين من العشر في العقار، وما سقت السَّماء أو كان سَيْحًا أو بَعْلًا، ففيه العُشر إذا بلغ خمسة أوسق، وما سقي بالرَّشاء والدَّالية، ففيه نصف العشر إذا بلغ خمسة أوسق. وفي كل خمس من الإبل سائمة شاة إلى أن تبلغ أربعًا وعشرين، فإذا زادت واحدة على أربع وعشرين ففيها ابنة مخاض، فإن لم توجد بنت مخاض فابن لبون ذكر إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وثلاثين، فإذا زادت على خمس وثلاثين ففيها ابنة لبون إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وأربعين، فإذا زادت على خمس وأربعين ففيها حقة طروقة إلى أن تبلغ ستين، فإن زادت على ستين واحدة ففيها جذعة إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وسبعين، فإن زادت على خمس وسبعين واحدة ففيها ابنتا لبون إلى أن تبلغ تسعين، فإن زادت على تسعين واحدة ففيها حقتان طروقتا الجمل إلى أن تبلغ عشرين ومائة، فما زاد ففي كل أربعين ابنة لبون، وفي كل خمسين حقة طروقة الجمل، وفي كل ثلاثين باقورة تبيع جذع أو جذعة، وفي كل أربعين باقورة بقرة. وفي كل أربعين شاة سائمة شاة إلى أن تبلغ عشرين ومائة، فإن زادت على عشرين ومائة واحدة ففيها شاتان إلى أن تبلغ مائتين، فإن زادت واحدة فثلاثة شياه إلى أن تبلغ ثلاثمائة، فما زاد ففي كل مائة شاة شاة. ولا تؤخذ في الصدقة هرمة، ولا عجفاء، ولا ذات عوار، ولا تيس الغنم، ولا يجمع بين متفرق، ولا يفرق بين مجتمع خيفة الصدقة، وما أخذ من الخليطين فإنهما يتراجعان بينهما بالسوية. وفي كل خمس أواق من الورق خمسة دراهم، فما زاد ففي كل أربعين درهمًا درهم، وليس فيما دون خمس أواق شيء، وفي كل أربعين دينارًا دينار )).

وإنَّ الصّدقةَ لا تحل لمحمّد ﷺ ولا لأهل بيته، وإنّما هي الزّكاة تزكى بها أنفسهم في فقراء المؤمنين، أو في سبيل الله.

وليس في رقيق ولا مزرعة ولا عمالها شيء، إذا كانت تؤدى صدقتها من العشر.

وليس في عبد المسلم ولا فرسه شيء.

وإنّ أكبر الكبائر عند اللّٰه يوم القيامة الإشراك بالله، وقتل النفس المؤمنة بغير الحق، والفرار في سبيل اللّٰه يوم الزحف، وعقوق الوالدين، ورمي المحصنة، وتعلّم السّحر، وأكل الربا، وأكل مال اليتيم.

وإنّ العمرة الحج الأصغر.

ولا يمسَّ القرآن إلا طاهر.

ولا طلاق قبل إملاك، ولا عتق حتى يبتاع.

ولا يصلينَّ أحدكم في ثوب واحد ليس على منكبه منه شيء، ولا يحتبين في ثوب واحد ليس بينه وبين السماء شيء، ولا يصلين أحدكم في ثوب واحد وشقه باد، ولا يصلين أحدكم عاقصًا شعره.

وإنّ من اعتبط مؤمنا قتلا عن بينة، فهو قود إلا أن يرضى أولياء المقتول.

وإنَّ في النفس الدية مائة من الإبل، وفي الأنف إذا أوعب جدعه الدية، وفي اللسان الدية، وفي الشفتين الدية، وفي البيضتين الدية، وفي الذكر الدية، وفي الصلب الدية، وفي العينين الدية، وفي الرجل الواحدة نصف الدية، وفي المأمومة ثلث الدية، وفي الجائفة ثلث الدية، وفي المنقلة خمس عشرة من الإبل، وفي كل إصبع من الأصابع من اليد والرجل عشر من الإبل، وفي السن خمس من الإبل، وفي الموضحة خمس من الإبل، وإن الرجل يقتل بالمرأة، وعلى أهل الذهب ألف دينار.

صحيح وجادة: رواه ابن حبان (٦٥٥٩) — واللفظ له —، والحاكم (١/٣٩٥–٣٩٦)، والبيهقي (٤/٨٩).

3956 — Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen a document containing the prescribed obligations, the established practices, and the blood-money rulings, and he sent it with ‘Amr ibn Hazm. It was read to the people of Yemen, and this is its text:

“From Muhammad the Prophet ﷺ to Shurahbil ibn ‘Abd Kulal, al-Harith ibn ‘Abd Kulal, Nu‘aym ibn ‘Abd Kulal, and the chiefs of Dhu Ru‘ayn, Ma‘afir, and Hamdan. To proceed:

Your messenger has returned, and you have been given from the war booty the fifth belonging to Allah. Also included is what Allah has prescribed upon the believers: one tenth on agricultural produce. Whatever is watered by rain, or flows naturally, or grows by natural moisture, then one tenth is due on it when it reaches five wasqs. And whatever is watered by lifting water or by irrigation equipment, then half of one tenth is due when it reaches five wasqs.

For every five grazing camels, one sheep is due until they reach twenty-four. If they increase by one over twenty-four, then one she-camel in her second year is due. If such a camel is not found, then a male camel in its third year is due until they reach thirty-five. If they increase beyond thirty-five, then one she-camel in her third year is due until forty-five. If they increase beyond forty-five, then one she-camel in her fourth year, fit for breeding, is due until sixty. If they increase by one over sixty, then one she-camel in her fifth year is due until seventy-five. If they increase by one over seventy-five, then two she-camels in their third year are due until ninety. If they increase by one over ninety, then two she-camels in their fourth year, fit for breeding, are due until one hundred and twenty. Whatever is more than that, then for every forty there is one she-camel in her third year due, and for every fifty there is one she-camel in her fourth year, fit for breeding, due. And for every thirty cattle, one yearling calf, male or female, is due; and for every forty cattle, one cow is due.

For every forty grazing sheep, one sheep is due until they reach one hundred and twenty. If they increase by one over one hundred and twenty, then two sheep are due until they reach two hundred. If they increase by one, then three sheep are due until they reach three hundred. Whatever is more than that, then for every hundred there is one sheep due.

An aged animal, an emaciated animal, one with a defect, or a breeding ram is not to be taken in charity. Separate herds are not to be combined, and combined herds are not to be separated, out of fear of charity. Whatever is taken from two mixed partners, then they are to settle it equally between themselves.

For every five awqiyahs of silver, five dirhams are due. Whatever is more than that, then for every forty dirhams, one dirham is due. There is nothing due on less than five awqiyahs of silver. And for every forty dinars, one dinar is due.

There is nothing due on slaves, nor on cultivated land, nor on its workers, if its due charity from the one tenth has already been paid.

There is nothing due on a Muslim’s slave or his horse.

The greatest major sins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are associating partners with Allah, killing a believing soul without right, fleeing from battle in the path of Allah on the day of combat, being undutiful to parents, falsely accusing a chaste woman, learning sorcery, consuming usury, and consuming the wealth of an orphan.

ʿUmrah is the lesser pilgrimage.

No one should touch the Qur’an except one who is in a state of purity.

There is no divorce before marriage, and no freeing of a slave until one owns him.

None of you should pray in a single garment with nothing of it over his shoulder. And none should sit wrapped up in a single garment with nothing between him and the sky. And none of you should pray in a single garment while a side of his body is exposed. And none of you should pray with his hair tied up.

Whoever deliberately kills a believer with clear proof established against him is subject to legal retaliation, unless the family of the slain person accepts otherwise.

For a life, the blood money is one hundred camels. For the nose, if it is completely severed, the full blood money is due. For the tongue, the full blood money is due. For the two lips, the full blood money is due. For the two testicles, the full blood money is due. For the male organ, the full blood money is due. For the backbone, the full blood money is due. For the two eyes, the full blood money is due. For one leg, half of the blood money is due. For a head wound reaching the brain, one third of the blood money is due. For a wound penetrating into the body cavity, one third of the blood money is due. For a fracture that displaces the bone, fifteen camels are due. For each finger of the hands and feet, ten camels are due. For each tooth, five camels are due. For an exposing wound, five camels are due. And a man is to be killed in retaliation for a woman. And upon the people of gold is one thousand dinars.”

٣٩٥٦ — عن أبي بكر بن محمد بن عمرو بن حزم، عن أبيه، عن جدّه: أن رسولَ اللّٰه ﷺ كتب إلى أهل اليمن بكتاب فيه الفرائض والسُّنن والدِّيات، وبعث به مع عمرو بن حزم، فقرئت على أهل اليمن، وهذه نسختها: (( من محمد النبي ﷺ إلى شرحبيل بن عبد كلال، والحارث بن عبد كلال، ونعيم بن عبد كلال، قيل ذي رُعَينٍ ومعافر وهمدان: أمّا بعد، فقد رجع رسولكم، وأعطيتم من الغنائم خُمس اللّٰه، وما كتب اللّٰه على المؤمنين من العشر في العقار، وما سقت السَّماء أو كان سَيْحًا أو بَعْلًا، ففيه العُشر إذا بلغ خمسة أوسق، وما سقي بالرَّشاء والدَّالية، ففيه نصف العشر إذا بلغ خمسة أوسق. وفي كل خمس من الإبل سائمة شاة إلى أن تبلغ أربعًا وعشرين، فإذا زادت واحدة على أربع وعشرين ففيها ابنة مخاض، فإن لم توجد بنت مخاض فابن لبون ذكر إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وثلاثين، فإذا زادت على خمس وثلاثين ففيها ابنة لبون إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وأربعين، فإذا زادت على خمس وأربعين ففيها حقة طروقة إلى أن تبلغ ستين، فإن زادت على ستين واحدة ففيها جذعة إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وسبعين، فإن زادت على خمس وسبعين واحدة ففيها ابنتا لبون إلى أن تبلغ تسعين، فإن زادت على تسعين واحدة ففيها حقتان طروقتا الجمل إلى أن تبلغ عشرين ومائة، فما زاد ففي كل أربعين ابنة لبون، وفي كل خمسين حقة طروقة الجمل، وفي كل ثلاثين باقورة تبيع جذع أو جذعة، وفي كل أربعين باقورة بقرة. وفي كل أربعين شاة سائمة شاة إلى أن تبلغ عشرين ومائة، فإن زادت على عشرين ومائة واحدة ففيها شاتان إلى أن تبلغ مائتين، فإن زادت واحدة فثلاثة شياه إلى أن تبلغ ثلاثمائة، فما زاد ففي كل مائة شاة شاة. ولا تؤخذ في الصدقة هرمة، ولا عجفاء، ولا ذات عوار، ولا تيس الغنم، ولا يجمع بين متفرق، ولا يفرق بين مجتمع خيفة الصدقة، وما أخذ من الخليطين فإنهما يتراجعان بينهما بالسوية. وفي كل خمس أواق من الورق خمسة دراهم، فما زاد ففي كل أربعين درهمًا درهم، وليس فيما دون خمس أواق شيء، وفي كل أربعين دينارًا دينار )).

وإنَّ الصّدقةَ لا تحل لمحمّد ﷺ ولا لأهل بيته، وإنّما هي الزّكاة تزكى بها أنفسهم في فقراء المؤمنين، أو في سبيل الله.

وليس في رقيق ولا مزرعة ولا عمالها شيء، إذا كانت تؤدى صدقتها من العشر.

وليس في عبد المسلم ولا فرسه شيء.

وإنّ أكبر الكبائر عند اللّٰه يوم القيامة الإشراك بالله، وقتل النفس المؤمنة بغير الحق، والفرار في سبيل اللّٰه يوم الزحف، وعقوق الوالدين، ورمي المحصنة، وتعلّم السّحر، وأكل الربا، وأكل مال اليتيم.

وإنّ العمرة الحج الأصغر.

ولا يمسَّ القرآن إلا طاهر.

٣٩٥٦ — عن أبي بكر بن محمد بن عمرو بن حزم، عن أبيه، عن جدّه: أن رسولَ اللّٰه ﷺ كتب إلى أهل اليمن بكتاب فيه الفرائض والسُّنن والدِّيات، وبعث به مع عمرو بن حزم، فقرئت على أهل اليمن، وهذه نسختها: (( من محمد النبي ﷺ إلى شرحبيل بن عبد كلال، والحارث بن عبد كلال، ونعيم بن عبد كلال، قيل ذي رُعَينٍ ومعافر وهمدان: أمّا بعد، فقد رجع رسولكم، وأعطيتم من الغنائم خُمس اللّٰه، وما كتب اللّٰه على المؤمنين من العشر في العقار، وما سقت السَّماء أو كان سَيْحًا أو بَعْلًا، ففيه العُشر إذا بلغ خمسة أوسق، وما سقي بالرَّشاء والدَّالية، ففيه نصف العشر إذا بلغ خمسة أوسق. وفي كل خمس من الإبل سائمة شاة إلى أن تبلغ أربعًا وعشرين، فإذا زادت واحدة على أربع وعشرين ففيها ابنة مخاض، فإن لم توجد بنت مخاض فابن لبون ذكر إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وثلاثين، فإذا زادت على خمس وثلاثين ففيها ابنة لبون إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وأربعين، فإذا زادت على خمس وأربعين ففيها حقة طروقة إلى أن تبلغ ستين، فإن زادت على ستين واحدة ففيها جذعة إلى أن تبلغ خمسًا وسبعين، فإن زادت على خمس وسبعين واحدة ففيها ابنتا لبون إلى أن تبلغ تسعين، فإن زادت على تسعين واحدة ففيها حقتان طروقتا الجمل إلى أن تبلغ عشرين ومائة، فما زاد ففي كل أربعين ابنة لبون، وفي كل خمسين حقة طروقة الجمل، وفي كل ثلاثين باقورة تبيع جذع أو جذعة، وفي كل أربعين باقورة بقرة. وفي كل أربعين شاة سائمة شاة إلى أن تبلغ عشرين ومائة، فإن زادت على عشرين ومائة واحدة ففيها شاتان إلى أن تبلغ مائتين، فإن زادت واحدة فثلاثة شياه إلى أن تبلغ ثلاثمائة، فما زاد ففي كل مائة شاة شاة. ولا تؤخذ في الصدقة هرمة، ولا عجفاء، ولا ذات عوار، ولا تيس الغنم، ولا يجمع بين متفرق، ولا يفرق بين مجتمع خيفة الصدقة، وما أخذ من الخليطين فإنهما يتراجعان بينهما بالسوية. وفي كل خمس أواق من الورق خمسة دراهم، فما زاد ففي كل أربعين درهمًا درهم، وليس فيما دون خمس أواق شيء، وفي كل أربعين دينارًا دينار )).

وإنَّ الصّدقةَ لا تحل لمحمّد ﷺ ولا لأهل بيته، وإنّما هي الزّكاة تزكى بها أنفسهم في فقراء المؤمنين، أو في سبيل الله.

وليس في رقيق ولا مزرعة ولا عمالها شيء، إذا كانت تؤدى صدقتها من العشر.

وليس في عبد المسلم ولا فرسه شيء.

وإنّ أكبر الكبائر عند اللّٰه يوم القيامة الإشراك بالله، وقتل النفس المؤمنة بغير الحق، والفرار في سبيل اللّٰه يوم الزحف، وعقوق الوالدين، ورمي المحصنة، وتعلّم السّحر، وأكل الربا، وأكل مال اليتيم.

وإنّ العمرة الحج الأصغر.

ولا يمسَّ القرآن إلا طاهر.

ولا طلاق قبل إملاك، ولا عتق حتى يبتاع.

ولا يصلينَّ أحدكم في ثوب واحد ليس على منكبه منه شيء، ولا يحتبين في ثوب واحد ليس بينه وبين السماء شيء، ولا يصلين أحدكم في ثوب واحد وشقه باد، ولا يصلين أحدكم عاقصًا شعره.

وإنّ من اعتبط مؤمنا قتلا عن بينة، فهو قود إلا أن يرضى أولياء المقتول.

وإنَّ في النفس الدية مائة من الإبل، وفي الأنف إذا أوعب جدعه الدية، وفي اللسان الدية، وفي الشفتين الدية، وفي البيضتين الدية، وفي الذكر الدية، وفي الصلب الدية، وفي العينين الدية، وفي الرجل الواحدة نصف الدية، وفي المأمومة ثلث الدية، وفي الجائفة ثلث الدية، وفي المنقلة خمس عشرة من الإبل، وفي كل إصبع من الأصابع من اليد والرجل عشر من الإبل، وفي السن خمس من الإبل، وفي الموضحة خمس من الإبل، وإن الرجل يقتل بالمرأة، وعلى أهل الذهب ألف دينار.

صحيح وجادة: رواه ابن حبان (٦٥٥٩) — واللفظ له —، والحاكم (١/٣٩٥–٣٩٦)، والبيهقي (٤/٨٩).

3956 — Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen a document containing the prescribed obligations, the established practices, and the blood-money rulings, and he sent it with ‘Amr ibn Hazm. It was read to the people of Yemen, and this is its text:

“From Muhammad the Prophet ﷺ to Shurahbil ibn ‘Abd Kulal, al-Harith ibn ‘Abd Kulal, Nu‘aym ibn ‘Abd Kulal, and the chiefs of Dhu Ru‘ayn, Ma‘afir, and Hamdan. To proceed:

Your messenger has returned, and you have been given from the war booty the fifth belonging to Allah. Also included is what Allah has prescribed upon the believers: one tenth on agricultural produce. Whatever is watered by rain, or flows naturally, or grows by natural moisture, then one tenth is due on it when it reaches five wasqs. And whatever is watered by lifting water or by irrigation equipment, then half of one tenth is due when it reaches five wasqs.

For every five grazing camels, one sheep is due until they reach twenty-four. If they increase by one over twenty-four, then one she-camel in her second year is due. If such a camel is not found, then a male camel in its third year is due until they reach thirty-five. If they increase beyond thirty-five, then one she-camel in her third year is due until forty-five. If they increase beyond forty-five, then one she-camel in her fourth year, fit for breeding, is due until sixty. If they increase by one over sixty, then one she-camel in her fifth year is due until seventy-five. If they increase by one over seventy-five, then two she-camels in their third year are due until ninety. If they increase by one over ninety, then two she-camels in their fourth year, fit for breeding, are due until one hundred and twenty. Whatever is more than that, then for every forty there is one she-camel in her third year due, and for every fifty there is one she-camel in her fourth year, fit for breeding, due. And for every thirty cattle, one yearling calf, male or female, is due; and for every forty cattle, one cow is due.

For every forty grazing sheep, one sheep is due until they reach one hundred and twenty. If they increase by one over one hundred and twenty, then two sheep are due until they reach two hundred. If they increase by one, then three sheep are due until they reach three hundred. Whatever is more than that, then for every hundred there is one sheep due.

An aged animal, an emaciated animal, one with a defect, or a breeding ram is not to be taken in charity. Separate herds are not to be combined, and combined herds are not to be separated, out of fear of charity. Whatever is taken from two mixed partners, then they are to settle it equally between themselves.

For every five awqiyahs of silver, five dirhams are due. Whatever is more than that, then for every forty dirhams, one dirham is due. There is nothing due on less than five awqiyahs of silver. And for every forty dinars, one dinar is due.

The charity is not lawful for Muhammad ﷺ nor for the people of his household. Rather, it is the zakat by which they purify themselves, and it is to be given to the poor among the believers or in the path of Allah.

There is nothing due on slaves, nor on cultivated land, nor on its workers, if its due charity from the one tenth has already been paid.

There is nothing due on a Muslim’s slave or his horse.

The greatest major sins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are associating partners with Allah, killing a believing soul without right, fleeing from battle in the path of Allah on the day of combat, being undutiful to parents, falsely accusing a chaste woman, learning sorcery, consuming usury, and consuming the wealth of an orphan.

ʿUmrah is the lesser pilgrimage.

No one should touch the Qur’an except one who is in a state of purity.

There is no divorce before marriage, and no freeing of a slave until one owns him.

None of you should pray in a single garment with nothing of it over his shoulder. And none should sit wrapped up in a single garment with nothing between him and the sky. And none of you should pray in a single garment while a side of his body is exposed. And none of you should pray with his hair tied up.

Whoever deliberately kills a believer with clear proof established against him is subject to legal retaliation, unless the family of the slain person accepts otherwise.

For a life, the blood money is one hundred camels. For the nose, if it is completely severed, the full blood money is due. For the tongue, the full blood money is due. For the two lips, the full blood money is due. For the two testicles, the full blood money is due. For the male organ, the full blood money is due. For the backbone, the full blood money is due. For the two eyes, the full blood money is due. For one leg, half of the blood money is due. For a head wound reaching the brain, one third of the blood money is due. For a wound penetrating into the body cavity, one third of the blood money is due. For a fracture that displaces the bone, fifteen camels are due. For each finger of the hands and feet, ten camels are due. For each tooth, five camels are due. For an exposing wound, five camels are due. And a man is to be killed in retaliation for a woman. And upon the people of gold is one thousand dinars.”

Authentic by transmitted manuscript form: Narrated by Ibn Hibban (6559) — and this is his wording — as well as al-Hakim (1/395–396) and al-Bayhaqi (4/89).

٣٩٥٧ — عن معاذ بن جبل، قال: بعثني رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ إلى اليمن، وأمرني أن آخذ من البقر من كلِّ أربعين مسنّة، ومن كلِّ ثلاثين تبيعًا أو تبيعة.

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (١٥٧٦)، والترمذي (٦٢٣)، والنسائي (٢٤٥٥)، وابن ماجه (١٨٠٣).

وقوله: «تبيعًا» وهي ما دخل في الثانية، وسمي تبيعًا لأنه فطم عن أمّه، فهو يتبعها.

وقوله: «مسنّة» وهي ما دخلت في الثالثة، وقيل الرابعة.

3957 — Mu‘adh ibn Jabal said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen and commanded me to take, from cattle, one two-year-old cow for every forty, and one one-year-old calf, male or female, for every thirty.

Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1576), al-Tirmidhi (623), al-Nasa’i (2455), and Ibn Majah (1803).

And the phrase “one-year-old calf” means an animal that has entered its second year. It is called that because it has been weaned from its mother and follows her.

And the phrase “two-year-old cow” means one that has entered its third year, and it was also said: its fourth year.

٣٩٥٨ — عن أنس، أن أبا بكر رضي اللّٰه عنه كتب له هذا الكتاب لما وّجهه إلى البحرين:

«بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ، هذه فريضةُ الصدقة التي فرض رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ على المسلمين، والتي أمر اللّٰه بها رسوله؛ فمن سُئلها من المسلمين على وجهها فليُعطها، ومن سُئل فوقها فلا يُعط...»

وجاء فيه: «وفي صدقة الغنم في سائمتها إذا كانت أربعين إلى عشرين ومائة شاة، فإذا زادت على عشرين ومائة إلى مائتين شاتان، فإذا زادت على مائتين إلى ثلاثمائة ففيها ثلاث شياه، فإذا زادت على ثلاثمائة ففي كل مائة شاة، فإذا كانت سائمة الرجل ناقصة من أربعين شاة واحدة فليس فيها صدقة إلا أن يشاء ربها، وفي الرِّقَة ربع العشر، فإن لم تكن إلا تسعين ومائة فليس فيها شيء إلا أن يشاء ربها».

صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٤٥٤).

3958 — Anas narrated that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote this document for him when he sent him to Bahrain:

“In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. This is the obligatory charity which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made binding upon the Muslims, and which Allah commanded His Messenger with. Whoever among the Muslims is asked for it according to what is due must give it, and whoever is asked for more than that should not give it…”

And in it came: “Regarding the charity due on grazing sheep: if they are from forty to one hundred and twenty, then one sheep is due. If they increase beyond one hundred and twenty up to two hundred, then two sheep are due. If they increase beyond two hundred up to three hundred, then three sheep are due. If they increase beyond three hundred, then for every hundred, one sheep is due. If a man’s grazing sheep are one short of forty, then no charity is due on them unless their owner wishes to give voluntarily. And regarding silver, one quarter of one tenth is due. If it is only one hundred and ninety, then nothing is due on it unless its owner wishes to give voluntarily.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1454).

٣٩٥٨ — عن أنس، أن أبا بكر رضي اللّٰه عنه كتب له هذا الكتاب لما وّجهه إلى البحرين:

«بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ، هذه فريضةُ الصدقة التي فرض رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ على المسلمين، والتي أمر اللّٰه بها رسوله؛ فمن سُئلها من المسلمين على وجهها فليُعطها، ومن سُئل فوقها فلا يُعط...»

وجاء فيه: «وفي صدقة الغنم في سائمتها إذا كانت أربعين إلى عشرين ومائة شاة، فإذا زادت على عشرين ومائة إلى مائتين شاتان، فإذا زادت على مائتين إلى ثلاثمائة ففيها ثلاث شياه، فإذا زادت على ثلاثمائة ففي كل مائة شاة، فإذا كانت سائمة الرجل ناقصة من أربعين شاة واحدة فليس فيها صدقة إلا أن يشاء ربها، وفي الرِّقَة ربع العشر، فإن لم تكن إلا تسعين ومائة فليس فيها شيء إلا أن يشاء ربها».

صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٤٥٤).

3958 — Anas narrated that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote this document for him when he sent him to Bahrain:

“In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. This is the obligatory charity which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made binding upon the Muslims, and which Allah commanded His Messenger with. Whoever among the Muslims is asked for it according to what is due must give it, and whoever is asked for more than that should not give it…”

And in it came: “Regarding the charity due on grazing sheep: if they are from forty to one hundred and twenty, then one sheep is due. If they increase beyond one hundred and twenty up to two hundred, then two sheep are due. If they increase beyond two hundred up to three hundred, then three sheep are due. If they increase beyond three hundred, then for every hundred, one sheep is due. If a man’s grazing sheep are one short of forty, then no charity is due on them unless their owner wishes to give voluntarily. And regarding silver, one quarter of one tenth is due. If it is only one hundred and ninety, then nothing is due on it unless its owner wishes to give voluntarily.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1454).

٣٩٦٠ — عن سويد بن غفلة قال:

سرت — أو قال: أخبرني من سار مع مصدق النبي ﷺ — فإذا في عهد رسول الله ﷺ:

«أَنْ لَا تَأْخُذْ مِنْ رَاضِعِ لَبَنٍ، وَلَا تَجْمَعْ بَيْنَ مُفْتَرِقٍ، وَلَا تُفَرِّقَ بَيْنَ مُجْتَمِعٍ».

وكان المصدق يأتي المياه حين ترد الغنم، فيقول:

أدوا صدقة أموالكم.

قال:

فعمد رجل منهم إلى ناقة كوماء، فجاء بها.

قال: قلت: يا أبا صالح، ما الكوماء؟

قال: عظيمة السنام.

قال: فأبى أن يقبلها.

قال الرجل:

إني أحب أن تأخذ خير إبلي.

فأبى أن يقبلها.

فخطم له أخرى دونها، فأبى أن يقبلها.

ثم خطم له أخرى دونها، فقبلها، وقال:

إني لآخذها، وإني لأخاف أن يجد علي رسول الله ﷺ، يقول لي:

«عَمَدْتَ إِلَى رَجُلٍ فَتَخَيَّرْتَ عَلَيْهِ إِبِلَهُ».

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٧٩)، والنسائي (٢٤٥٩).

3960 — Suwayd ibn Ghafalah said:

I traveled—or he said: someone who traveled with the zakat collector of the Prophet ﷺ informed me—that in the written instructions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ it stated:

“Do not take a milk-suckling animal, do not combine separate herds, and do not separate a combined herd.”

The collector would come to the watering places when the livestock arrived and say:

“Give the zakat due on your property.”

A man among them then brought a large-humped she-camel.

I asked:

“O Abū Ṣāliḥ, what does kawmāʾ mean?”

He replied:

“A camel with a large hump.”

The collector refused to accept it.

The man said:

“I would like you to take the best of my camels.”

But he refused to accept it.

Then he haltered another camel of lower quality, but the collector refused that one as well.

Then he haltered another one below that in quality, and the collector accepted it, saying:

“I will take this one, though I fear that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ may be displeased with me and say:

‘You went to a man and deliberately selected the choicest of his camels.’”

Hasan: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1579) and al-Nasāʾī (2459).

٣٩٦١ — عن أبي هريرة، أن رسولَ اللّٰه ﷺ قال: «ليس على المسلم في عبده ولا في فرسه صدقة».

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٣٧)، ومسلم في الزكاة (٩٨٢)، والبخاري في الزكاة (١٤٦٣).

وعند مسلم: «ليس في العبد صدقة إلا صدقة الفطر».

3961 — Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A Muslim owes no charity on his slave or on his horse.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (37), Muslim in the Book of Zakat (982), and al-Bukhari in the Book of Zakat (1463).

And in the version of Muslim: “There is no charity due on a slave except the charity of the breaking of the fast.”

3962 — ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have exempted horses and slaves. So give the charity due on silver: from every forty dirhams, one dirham. There is nothing due on one hundred and ninety. Once it reaches two hundred, then five dirhams are due.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1574), al-Tirmidhi (620), and al-Nasa’i (2478).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٧٤)، والترمذي (٦٢٠)، والنسائي (٢٤٧٨).

3962 — ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have exempted horses and slaves. So give the charity due on silver: from every forty dirhams, one dirham. There is nothing due on one hundred and ninety. Once it reaches two hundred, then five dirhams are due.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1574), al-Tirmidhi (620), and al-Nasa’i (2478).

٣٩٦٣ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ: «ما من صاحب ذهب ولا فضة لا يؤدي منها حقها، إلا إذا كان يوم القيامة صُفحت له صفائح من نار، فأُحمي عليها في نار جهنم، فيُكوى بها جنبه وجبينه وظهره، كلما بردت أُعيدت له، في يوم كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة، حتى يُقضى بين العباد، فيرى سبيله إما إلى الجنة وإما إلى النار».

قيل: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فالإبل؟ قال: «ولا صاحب إبل لا يؤدي منها حقها، ومن حقها حلبها يوم وردها، إلا إذا كان يوم القيامة بُطح لها بقاع قرقر، أوفر ما كانت، لا يفقد منها فصيلًا واحدًا، تطؤه بأخفافها وتعضه بأفواهها، كلما مر عليه أولاها رُد عليه أخراها، في يوم كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة، حتى يُقضى بين العباد، فيرى سبيله إما إلى الجنة وإما إلى النار».

قيل: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فالبقر والغنم؟ قال: «ولا صاحب بقر ولا غنم لا يؤدي منها حقها، إلا إذا كان يوم القيامة بُطح لها بقاع قرقر، لا يفقد منها شيئًا، ليس فيها عقصاء ولا جلحاء ولا عضباء؛ تنطحه بقرونها وتطؤه بأظلافها، كلما مر عليه أولاها رُد عليه أخراها، في يوم كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة، حتى يُقضى بين العباد، فيرى سبيله إما إلى الجنة وإما إلى النار».

قيل: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فالخيل؟ قال: «الخيل ثلاثة: هي لرجل وزر، وهي لرجل ستر، وهي لرجل أجر. فأما التي هي له وزر، فرجل ربطها رياء وفخرًا ونواء على أهل الإسلام، فهي له وزر. وأما التي هي له ستر، فرجل ربطها في سبيل اللّٰه ثم لم ينس حق اللّٰه في ظهورها ولا رقابها، فهي له ستر. وأما التي هي له أجر، فرجل ربطها في سبيل اللّٰه لأهل الإسلام في مرج أو روضة، فما أكلت من ذلك المرج أو الروضة من شيء إلا كتب له عدد ما أكلت حسنات، وكتب له عدد أرواثها وأبوالها حسنات، ولا تقطع طولها فاستنت شرفًا أو شرفين إلا كتب اللّٰه له عدد آثارها وأرواثها حسنات، ولا مر بها صاحبها على نهر فشربت منه ولا يريد أن يسقيها إلا كتب اللّٰه له عدد ما شربت حسنات».

قيل: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فالحمر؟ قال: «ما أُنزل علي في الحمر شيء إلا هذه الآية الفاذة الجامعة: ﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ ۝ وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ﴾ [الزلزلة: ٧-٨]».

متفق عليه: رواه مسلم (٩٨٧)، والبخاري (٢٣٧١)، واللفظ لمسلم.

3963 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay what is due on it except that, on the Day of Resurrection, sheets of fire will be made for him, heated in the Fire of Hell, and his side, forehead, and back will be branded with them. Every time they cool down, they will be reheated for him during a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire.”

It was said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what about camels?” He said, “And no owner of camels who does not give their due — and part of their due is that they are milked on the day they come to water — except that on the Day of Resurrection he will be thrown down for them on a broad, level plain, with the herd as full as it ever was, not missing even a single young one. They will trample him with their hooves and bite him with their mouths. Every time the first of them passes over him, the last of them will be brought back over him again, during a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire.”

It was said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what about cattle and sheep?” He said, “And no owner of cattle or sheep who does not give their due except that on the Day of Resurrection he will be thrown down for them on a broad, level plain, not missing any of them. None of them will be twisted-horned, hornless, or broken-horned. They will gore him with their horns and trample him with their hooves. Every time the first of them passes over him, the last of them will be brought back over him again, during a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire.”

It was said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what about horses?” He said, “Horses are of three kinds: for one man they are a burden of sin, for another they are a shield, and for another they are a reward. As for the one for whom they are a burden of sin, he is a man who keeps them out of showing off, pride, and hostility against the people of Islam, so they are a burden of sin for him. As for the one for whom they are a shield, he is a man who keeps them in the path of Allah, then does not forget the right of Allah concerning their backs and their necks, so they are a protection for him. As for the one for whom they are a reward, he is a man who keeps them in the path of Allah for the people of Islam in a meadow or garden. Whatever they eat from that meadow or garden, good deeds are written for him equal to the number of what they eat. And good deeds are written for him equal to the number of their droppings and urine. If they break their tether and run over one hill or two hills, good deeds are written for him equal to the number of their tracks and droppings. And whenever their owner passes by a river and they drink from it, even though he did not intend to water them, good deeds are written for him equal to the number of what they drank.”

It was said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what about donkeys?” He said, “Nothing has been revealed to me regarding donkeys except this all-encompassing verse: ‘So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.’” [al-Zalzalah 99:7–8]

Agreed upon: Narrated by Muslim (987) and al-Bukhari (2371), and this wording is from Muslim.

قيل: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فالإبل؟ قال: «ولا صاحب إبل لا يؤدي منها حقها، ومن حقها حلبها يوم وردها، إلا إذا كان يوم القيامة بُطح لها بقاع قرقر، أوفر ما كانت، لا يفقد منها فصيلًا واحدًا، تطؤه بأخفافها وتعضه بأفواهها، كلما مر عليه أولاها رُد عليه أخراها، في يوم كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة، حتى يُقضى بين العباد، فيرى سبيله إما إلى الجنة وإما إلى النار».

قيل: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فالبقر والغنم؟ قال: «ولا صاحب بقر ولا غنم لا يؤدي منها حقها، إلا إذا كان يوم القيامة بُطح لها بقاع قرقر، لا يفقد منها شيئًا، ليس فيها عقصاء ولا جلحاء ولا عضباء؛ تنطحه بقرونها وتطؤه بأظلافها، كلما مر عليه أولاها رُد عليه أخراها، في يوم كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة، حتى يُقضى بين العباد، فيرى سبيله إما إلى الجنة وإما إلى النار».

قيل: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فالخيل؟ قال: «الخيل ثلاثة: هي لرجل وزر، وهي لرجل ستر، وهي لرجل أجر. فأما التي هي له وزر، فرجل ربطها رياء وفخرًا ونواء على أهل الإسلام، فهي له وزر. وأما التي هي له ستر، فرجل ربطها في سبيل اللّٰه ثم لم ينس حق اللّٰه في ظهورها ولا رقابها، فهي له ستر. وأما التي هي له أجر، فرجل ربطها في سبيل اللّٰه لأهل الإسلام في مرج أو روضة، فما أكلت من ذلك المرج أو الروضة من شيء إلا كتب له عدد ما أكلت حسنات، وكتب له عدد أرواثها وأبوالها حسنات، ولا تقطع طولها فاستنت شرفًا أو شرفين إلا كتب اللّٰه له عدد آثارها وأرواثها حسنات، ولا مر بها صاحبها على نهر فشربت منه ولا يريد أن يسقيها إلا كتب اللّٰه له عدد ما شربت حسنات».

قيل: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فالحمر؟ قال: «ما أُنزل علي في الحمر شيء إلا هذه الآية الفاذة الجامعة: ﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ ۝ وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ﴾ [الزلزلة: ٧-٨]».

متفق عليه: رواه مسلم (٩٨٧)، والبخاري (٢٣٧١)، واللفظ لمسلم.

3963 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay what is due on it except that, on the Day of Resurrection, sheets of fire will be made for him, heated in the Fire of Hell, and his side, forehead, and back will be branded with them. Every time they cool down, they will be reheated for him during a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire.”

It was said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what about camels?” He said, “And no owner of camels who does not give their due — and part of their due is that they are milked on the day they come to water — except that on the Day of Resurrection he will be thrown down for them on a broad, level plain, with the herd as full as it ever was, not missing even a single young one. They will trample him with their hooves and bite him with their mouths. Every time the first of them passes over him, the last of them will be brought back over him again, during a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire.”

It was said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what about cattle and sheep?” He said, “And no owner of cattle or sheep who does not give their due except that on the Day of Resurrection he will be thrown down for them on a broad, level plain, not missing any of them. None of them will be twisted-horned, hornless, or broken-horned. They will gore him with their horns and trample him with their hooves. Every time the first of them passes over him, the last of them will be brought back over him again, during a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire.”

It was said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what about horses?” He said, “Horses are of three kinds: for one man they are a burden of sin, for another they are a shield, and for another they are a reward. As for the one for whom they are a burden of sin, he is a man who keeps them out of showing off, pride, and hostility against the people of Islam, so they are a burden of sin for him. As for the one for whom they are a shield, he is a man who keeps them in the path of Allah, then does not forget the right of Allah concerning their backs and their necks, so they are a protection for him. As for the one for whom they are a reward, he is a man who keeps them in the path of Allah for the people of Islam in a meadow or garden. Whatever they eat from that meadow or garden, good deeds are written for him equal to the number of what they eat. And good deeds are written for him equal to the number of their droppings and urine. If they break their tether and run over one hill or two hills, good deeds are written for him equal to the number of their tracks and droppings. And whenever their owner passes by a river and they drink from it, even though he did not intend to water them, good deeds are written for him equal to the number of what they drank.”

It was said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what about donkeys?” He said, “Nothing has been revealed to me regarding donkeys except this all-encompassing verse: ‘So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.’” [al-Zalzalah 99:7–8]

Agreed upon: Narrated by Muslim (987) and al-Bukhari (2371), and this wording is from Muslim.

٣٩٦٤ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جدِّه، عن النبي ﷺ قال: «لا جَلَبَ ولا جَنَبَ، ولا تؤخذ صدقاتهم إلا في دورهم».

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٩١) وصحّحه ابن خزيمة (٢٢٨٠). وأحمد (٧٠٢٤).

قوله: (( لا جلب ولاجنب)) : أن تصدق الماشية في مواضعها، ولا تجلب إلى المصدّق.

والجنب: لا يجنب أصحابها، يقول: لا يكون الرجل بأقصى مواضع الصّدقة فتُجنب إليه، ولكن تؤخذ في موضعه

3964 — ‘Amr ibn Shu‘ayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet, who said: “There is to be no driving of livestock in and no sending them from afar, and their charities are only to be taken in their own places.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1591), authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (2280), and also by Ahmad (7024).

Its meaning is: the livestock are to be assessed for charity in their own locations, and they are not to be driven to the collector.

And it also means: their owners are not to be made to bring them from far-off places. A man should not be at the far edge of the collection area and have the animals driven to him. Rather, they are taken where they are.

٣٩٦٥ — عن أم المؤمنين عائشة قالت: قال رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ: «تؤخذ صدقات أهل البادية على مياههم وبأفنيتهم».

حسن: رواه الطبرانيّ في “الأوسط” (مجمع البحرين ١٣٦٠).

يستفاد من أحاديث الباب أن المصدق هو الذي يأتي أصحاب الصدقات، ويجبيها منهم على مياههم، لكون ذلك أسهل لأصحاب المواشي.

3965 — The Mother of the Believers, ‘A’ishah, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “The charities of the desert people are to be taken at their watering places and in their courtyards.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (Majma‘ al-Bahrayn, 1360).

What is understood from the hadiths of this chapter is that the collector is the one who goes to the people who owe charity and takes it from them at their own watering places, because that is easier for the owners of livestock.

٣٩٦٦ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: غدوتُ إلى رسولِ اللّٰه ﷺ بعبدِ الله بن أبي طلحة يُحنِّكه، فوافيتُه في يده المِيسَمُ يَسِمُ إبلَ الصدقة.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٥٠٢)، ومسلم (٢١١٩/١١٢).

والوسم من وَسَمَ يَسِمُ وَسْمًا: إذا أثَّر فيه بكيٍّ، والمِيسَم: الحديدة التي يُكوى بها.

3966 — Anas ibn Malik said: I went early to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Talhah so that he could perform taḥnīk for him, and I found him holding the branding iron, branding the camels of charity.

Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (1502), Muslim (2119).

Branding comes from the verb meaning to mark something by cauterizing it. The mīsam is the iron instrument used for branding.

٣٩٦٧ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: دخلتُ على النبي ﷺ بأخٍ لي يُحنِّكه، وهو في مِرْبَدٍ له، فرأيتُه يَسِمُ شاةً. حسبتُه قال: في آذانها.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٥٤٢)، ومسلم (٢١١٩/١١١)، واللفظ للبخاري.

3967 — Anas ibn Malik said: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ with a brother of mine so that he could perform taḥnīk for him, while he was in an enclosure of his, and I saw him branding a sheep. I think he said: on its ears.

Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (5542), Muslim (2119), and this is the wording of al-Bukhari.

٣٩٦٧ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: دخلتُ على النبي ﷺ بأخٍ لي يُحنِّكه، وهو في مِرْبَدٍ له، فرأيتُه يَسِمُ شاةً. حسبتُه قال: في آذانها.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٥٤٢)، ومسلم (٢١١٩/١١١)، واللفظ للبخاري.

3967 — Anas ibn Malik said: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ with a brother of mine so that he could perform taḥnīk for him, while he was in an enclosure of his, and I saw him branding a sheep. I think he said: on its ears.

Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (5542), Muslim (2119), and this is the wording of al-Bukhari.

3968 — Anas reported that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote this letter for him when he sent him to Bahrain: “This is the obligation of charity that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made obligatory upon the Muslims.” Then he mentioned the full document, and in it was:

“Regarding silver, one-quarter of one-tenth is due. If it is only one hundred and ninety, then nothing is due on it unless its owner wishes.”

Authentic: al-Bukhari (1454).

Riqqah means pure silver, whether minted into coins or not.

The phrase “if it is only one hundred and ninety” might make it sound as though zakat becomes due on anything above one hundred and ninety before reaching two hundred, but that is not the meaning. Ninety was mentioned because it is the last full ten before two hundred, to show that there is no zakat on anything less than two hundred. This is also proven by the hadith: “There is no charity due on less than five uqiyyahs.”

٣٩٦٩ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ: (( ليس فيما دون خمسِ ذَوْدٍ صدقة، وليس فيما دون خمسِ أواقٍ صدقة، وليس فيما دون خمسةِ أوسقٍ صدقة )).

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (١)، والبخاري (١٤٤٧)، ومسلم (٩٧٩).

وقوله: (( خمسِ ذودٍ )) بإضافة ذود إلى خمس، وقد روي أيضًا بتنوين خمس، ويكون ذود بدلًا منه.

والذَّود في اللغة: من الثلاثة إلى العشرة، لا واحد له من لفظه، وإنما يقال في الواحد: بعير.

وقوله: (( خمس ذود )) مثل قولك: خمسة أبعرة، وخمسة جمال، وخمس نوق.

وقوله: (( خمس أواقٍ )) بالتنوين، وفي رواية: (( أواقي )) بإثبات الياء، وكلاهما صحيح.

والأوقية: بضم الهمزة وتشديد الياء، وجمعها: أواقي، وأواقٍ.

وأجمع أهل الحديث والفقه وأئمة اللغة على أن الأوقية الشرعية أربعون درهمًا، وهي أوقية الحجاز. ولا خلاف بين أهل العلم على أن نصاب الفضة مائتا درهم، وهو اليوم نحو ستمائة غرام، فإن كان أقل من ذلك فلا زكاة عليه.

وقوله: (( خمسة أوسق )): الأوسق جمع وسق، وفيه لغتان: فتح الواو، وهو المشهور، وكسرها. وأصلها في اللغة: الحمل.

والوسق: ستون صاعًا، وخمسة أوسق = ٣٠٠ صاع.

ومقدار الصاع النبوي نحو ٢.٥ كغ.

وعلى هذا يكون وزن خمسة أوسق نحو ٧٥٠ كغ.

3969 — Abu Saʿid al-Khudri said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no charity due on fewer than five camels, no charity due on fewer than five uqiyyahs, and no charity due on fewer than five awsuq.”

Agreed upon: Malik (1), al-Bukhari (1447), Muslim (979).

The phrase “five camels” uses the word dhawd, which in Arabic refers to a small number of camels, usually from three to ten.

The phrase “five uqiyyahs” is also narrated as awāqī, and both are correct.

The legal uqiyyah is agreed upon by hadith scholars, jurists, and language scholars to equal forty dirhams, which means that the nisab of silver is two hundred dirhams. In present-day measure, that is about six hundred grams. If it is less than that, then no zakat is due on it.

The phrase “five awsuq” means five wasqs. One wasq equals sixty sāʿs, so five awsuq equal three hundred sāʿs.

The Prophetic sāʿ is approximately 2.5 kilograms, so five awsuq weigh about 750 kilograms.

3973 — ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have excused horses and slaves, so bring the charity due on silver: from every forty dirhams, one dirham. There is nothing due on one hundred and ninety, but when it reaches two hundred, then five dirhams are due on it.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1574), al-Tirmidhi (620), al-Nasa’i (2478), Ibn Majah (1790), and Ahmad (711, 984).

english_source:
3976 — ʿAli ibn Abi Talib reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “If you have two hundred dirhams and a year passes over them, then five dirhams are due on them. And nothing is due on you in gold until you have twenty dinars. If you have twenty dinars and a year passes over them, then half a dinar is due on them. Whatever is more than that is according to this calculation.”

Hasan: Abu Dawud (1573).

The nisab of gold is twenty dinars, which is about 85 grams today, and it is also said to be about 92 grams.

The nisab of silver is two hundred dirhams, which is about 595 grams today.

Whoever has paper currency should assess it according to silver, because that is more beneficial for the poor. If its value reaches the nisab of silver and a full year passes over it, then zakat becomes obligatory on it.

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٧٣).

3976 — ʿAli ibn Abi Talib reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “If you have two hundred dirhams and a year passes over them, then five dirhams are due on them. And nothing is due on you in gold until you have twenty dinars. If you have twenty dinars and a year passes over them, then half a dinar is due on them. Whatever is more than that is according to this calculation.”

Hasan: Abu Dawud (1573).

The nisab of gold is twenty dinars, which is about 85 grams today, and it is also said to be about 92 grams.

The nisab of silver is two hundred dirhams, which is about 595 grams today.

Whoever has paper currency should assess it according to silver, because that is more beneficial for the poor. If its value reaches the nisab of silver and a full year passes over it, then zakat becomes obligatory on it.

٣٩٧٨ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جدِّه قال: سُئل رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ عن اللقطة فقال: (( ما كان في طريقٍ مَأتيٍّ أو في قريةٍ عامرةٍ فعرِّفها سنة، فإن جاء صاحبُها وإلا فلك، وما لم يكن في طريقٍ مأتيٍّ ولا في قريةٍ عامرةٍ ففيه وفي الركاز الخمس )).

حسن: رواه النسائي (٢٤٩٤)، وأبو داود (١٧١٢)، واللفظ للنسائي.

وقوله: (( مَأتيّ )) كـ مرميّ، وهو طريقٌ مسلوك.

وقوله: (( وفي الركاز الخمس )): الركاز هو الكنز الجاهلي المدفون في الأرض، وإنما وجب فيه الخمس لكثرة نفعه وسهولة أخذه.

3978 — ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about found property, and he said: “Whatever is found on a traveled road or in an inhabited village, announce it for one year. If its owner comes, then give it to him; otherwise it is yours. But whatever is not found on a traveled road nor in an inhabited village, then one-fifth is due on it and on buried treasure.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (2494) and Abu Dawud (1712), and this is the wording of al-Nasa’i.

The phrase “a traveled road” means a road that people use.

Rikaz means pre-Islamic treasure buried in the ground. One-fifth is due on it because of its great benefit and the ease of obtaining it.

٣٩٧٩ — عن جابر قال: قال رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ: (( السائبة — وقال خلف بن الوليد: السائمة — جبار، والجبُّ جبار، والمعدن جبار، وفي الركاز الخمس )).

قال الشعبي: الركاز: الكنز العادي.

حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (١٤٥٩٢، ١٤٨١٠)، والبزار “كشف الأستار” (٨٩٤).

3979 — Jabir said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “An unattended animal — and Khalaf ibn al-Walīd said: a grazing animal — is without liability; a well is without liability; a mine is without liability; and on buried treasure one-fifth is due.”

Al-Shaʿbi said: Rikaz means ancient buried treasure.

Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (14592, 14810) and al-Bazzar in Kashf al-Astar (894).

٣٩٨٠ — عن زينب امرأة عبد الله قالت: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( تصدّقن يا معشر النساء، ولو من حُليكنّ )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٤٦٦)، ومسلم (١٠٠٠).

قال ابن العربي: ظاهر هذا الحديث يدلّ على أنه لا زكاة في الحلي؛ لأن النبي ﷺ أمر بالصدقة منه، ولو كانت الزكاة واجبة فيه لما جعله مثالًا لصدقة التطوّع.

وقال الترمذي: اختلف أهل العلم في الحلي:

فقال بعض الصحابة والتابعين: فيه زكاة إذا كان ذهبًا أو فضة (ومنهم سفيان الثوري وعبد الله بن المبارك).

وقال آخرون من الصحابة: لا زكاة فيه (ومنهم ابن عمر، وعائشة، وجابر، وأنس)، وبه قال مالك والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق.

3980 — Zaynab, the wife of ʿAbdullah, reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Give charity, O women, even if it is from your jewelry.”

Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (1466) and Muslim (1000).

Ibn al-ʿArabi said: The apparent meaning of this hadith indicates that there is no zakat on jewelry, because the Prophet ﷺ encouraged voluntary charity from it. If zakat were obligatory on it, he would not have used it as an example of voluntary charity.

Al-Tirmidhi said: Scholars differed on this issue:

Some Companions and Followers held that zakat is due on gold and silver jewelry, including Sufyan al-Thawri and ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mubarak.

Others among the Companions said there is no zakat on jewelry, including Ibn ʿUmar, ʿA’ishah, Jabir, and Anas; and this is the view of Malik, al-Shafiʿi, Ahmad, and Ishaq.

٣٩٨١ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جدّه: أن امرأةً أتت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ومعها ابنةٌ لها، وفي يد ابنتها مسكتان غليظتان من ذهب، فقال لها: (( أتعطين زكاة هذا؟ )) قالت: لا. قال: (( أيسرك أن يسوّرك اللّٰه بهما يوم القيامة سوارين من نار؟! )) قال: فخلعتهما فألقتهما إلى النبي ﷺ وقالت: هما لله عز وجل ولرسوله.

٣٩٨٢ — عن عبد الله بن شداد بن الهاد قال: دخلنا على عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ فقالت: دخل عليّ رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فرأى في يدي فتخاتٍ من ورق فقال: (( ما هذا يا عائشة؟ )) فقلت: صنعتهن أتزيّن لك يا رسول الله ﷺ. قال: (( أتؤدين زكاتهن؟ )) قلت: لا، أو ما شاء الله. قال: (( هو حسبك من النار )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٦٥).

٣٩٨٣ — عن أم سلمة قالت: كنت ألبس أوضاحًا من ذهب فقلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، أكنز هو؟ فقال ﷺ: (( ما بلغ أن تؤدى زكاته فزُكّي فليس بكنز )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٦٤).

اختلف العلماء في زكاة الحلي:

من أوجبها استدل بهذه الأحاديث.

ومن أسقطها استدل بأحاديث أخرى وبأن الحلي للاستعمال كأمتعة البيت.

 والاحتياط: إخراج الزكاة.

3983 — Umm Salamah said: I used to wear gold jewelry and asked: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, is this considered hoarded wealth? He said: “Whatever reaches the amount on which zakat is due and its zakat is paid is not considered hoarded wealth.”

Hasan: Abu Dawud (1564).

Scholars differed regarding zakat on jewelry:

Those who say it is obligatory rely on the warning hadiths.

Those who say it is not obligatory view jewelry as personal use items like household goods.

Conclusion: The safer opinion is to pay zakat on it.

٣٩٨٤ — عن ابن عمر، عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال:

(( فيما سقت السماء والعيون أو كان عثريًا العشر، وما سُقي بالنضح نصف العشر )).

صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٤٨٣).

وفي بعض طرق الحديث:

(( فيما سقت السماء والأنهار والعيون أو كان بعلاً العشر، وفيما سُقي بالسواني أو النضح نصف العشر )).

رواه أبو داود (١٥٩٦) وغيره.

قوله: (( أو كان عثريًا )) العثري من الزرع: هو الذي يشرب بعروقه من غير سقي، واشتقاقه من العاثور، وهي الساقية التي يجري فيها الماء؛ لأن الماشي يعثر فيها. ومنه الذي يشرب من الأنهار بغير مؤنة، أو يشرب بعروقه، كأن يُغرس في أرض يكون الماء قريبًا من وجهها فيصل إليه عروق الشجر فيستغني عن السقي. انظر: الفتح (٣/٣٤٩).

وقوله: (( بعلاً )) نقل أبو داود عن وكيع: البعل هو الذي ينبت من ماء السماء. ونقل عن النضر بن شميل: البعل ماء المطر. والخلاصة: هو ما شرب بعروقه ولم يُتعب في سقيه.

والنضح: هو السقي بالرشاء.

ويفهم مما تقدم أن النبي ﷺ جعل الصدقة فيما خفّت مؤنته وكثرت منفعته على التضعيف توسعة على الفقراء، وجعل ما كثرت مؤنته على التنصيف رفقًا بأرباب الأموال.

والسواني: جمع السانية، وهي البعير الذي يُستقى عليه.

3984 — Ibn ʿUmar reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:

“Whatever is watered by the sky, springs, or is naturally watered through its roots, then one-tenth is due. And whatever is watered by manual irrigation, then half of one-tenth is due.”

Authentic: narrated by al-Bukhari (1483).

And in some routes of the hadith:

“Whatever is watered by the sky, rivers, and springs, or is naturally watered, then one-tenth is due. And whatever is watered by water-wheels or manual irrigation, then half of one-tenth is due.”

Narrated by Abu Dawud (1596) and others.

The phrase “or is naturally watered” refers to crops that drink through their roots without direct irrigation. This includes what takes water from rivers without expense, or trees planted where underground water is close enough for roots to reach it, so that irrigation is unnecessary. See: Fath al-Bari (3/349).

The phrase “baʿl” was explained by Abu Dawud from Wakiʿ as that which grows from rainwater. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: it means rainwater. In short, it refers to what drinks through its roots without irrigation effort.

“Al-nadḥ” means irrigation by drawing water with ropes.

What is understood from this is that the Prophet ﷺ made the zakat larger for crops whose cost is light and whose benefit is greater, as an ease for the poor, and made it smaller for crops whose cost is high, as a mercy to the owners of wealth.

“Al-sawani” is the plural of saniyah, meaning a camel used to draw water.

٣٩٨٤ — عن ابن عمر، عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال:

(( فيما سقت السماء والعيون أو كان عثريًا العشر، وما سُقي بالنضح نصف العشر )).

صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٤٨٣).

وفي بعض طرق الحديث:

(( فيما سقت السماء والأنهار والعيون أو كان بعلاً العشر، وفيما سُقي بالسواني أو النضح نصف العشر )).

رواه أبو داود (١٥٩٦) وغيره.

قوله: (( أو كان عثريًا )) العثري من الزرع: هو الذي يشرب بعروقه من غير سقي، واشتقاقه من العاثور، وهي الساقية التي يجري فيها الماء؛ لأن الماشي يعثر فيها. ومنه الذي يشرب من الأنهار بغير مؤنة، أو يشرب بعروقه، كأن يُغرس في أرض يكون الماء قريبًا من وجهها فيصل إليه عروق الشجر فيستغني عن السقي. انظر: الفتح (٣/٣٤٩).

وقوله: (( بعلاً )) نقل أبو داود عن وكيع: البعل هو الذي ينبت من ماء السماء. ونقل عن النضر بن شميل: البعل ماء المطر. والخلاصة: هو ما شرب بعروقه ولم يُتعب في سقيه.

والنضح: هو السقي بالرشاء.

ويفهم مما تقدم أن النبي ﷺ جعل الصدقة فيما خفّت مؤنته وكثرت منفعته على التضعيف توسعة على الفقراء، وجعل ما كثرت مؤنته على التنصيف رفقًا بأرباب الأموال.

والسواني: جمع السانية، وهي البعير الذي يُستقى عليه.

“Whatever is watered by the sky, springs, or is naturally watered through its roots, then one-tenth is due. And whatever is watered by manual irrigation, then half of one-tenth is due.”

Authentic: narrated by al-Bukhari (1483).

“Whatever is watered by the sky, rivers, and springs, or is naturally watered, then one-tenth is due. And whatever is watered by water-wheels or manual irrigation, then half of one-tenth is due.”

٣٩٨٥ — عن جابر بن عبد الله أنه سمع النبي ﷺ يقول:

(( فيما سقت الأنهار والغيم العشور، وفيما سُقي بالسّانية نصف العشر )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩٨١).

قوله: (( فيما سقت الأنهار والغيم العشور )) العشور: بضم العين، جمع عُشر، والغيم هو المطر.

“One-tenth from what is watered by rain and what is naturally watered, and half of one-tenth from what is watered by irrigation devices.”

Hasan: narrated by Ibn Majah (1818) and al-Nasa’i (2492).

٣٩٨٩ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال:

(( جاء هلالٌ أحد بني متعان إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بعشور نحلٍ له، وكان سأله أن يحمي له واديًا يقال له سَلَبَة، فحمى له رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ذلك الوادي. فلما ولي عمر بن الخطاب رضي اللّٰه عنه، كتب سفيان بن وهب إلى عمر بن الخطاب يسأله عن ذلك، فكتب عمر رضي اللّٰه عنه: إن أدّى إليك ما كان يؤدّي إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ من عشور نحله فاحمِ له سَلَبَة، وإلا فإنما هو ذبابُ غيثٍ يأكله من يشاء )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٦٠٠) واللفظ له، والنسائي (٢٤٩٨).

3989 — ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr said:

Hilal, one of Banu Mutʿan, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the tithe of his bees. He had asked him to reserve for him a valley called Salabah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ protected that valley for him. When ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab became ruler, Sufyan ibn Wahb wrote to ʿUmar asking him about that, so ʿUmar wrote: “If he gives you what he used to give to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the tithes of his bees, then reserve Salabah for him. Otherwise, they are only rain-flies, eaten by whoever wishes.”

Hasan: narrated by Abu Dawud (1600), and this is his wording, and by al-Nasa’i (2498).

3990 — Abu Humayd al-Saʿidi said: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ on the expedition of Tabuk. When he came to Wadi al-Qura, there was a woman in her garden, and the Prophet ﷺ said to his companions:

“Estimate it.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ estimated it as ten awsuq, and said to her:

“Keep count of what comes out from it.”

When we came to Tabuk, he said:

“Tonight a strong wind will blow, so none of you should stand up, and whoever has a camel with him should tie it.”

So we tied them, and a strong wind blew. A man stood up, and the wind threw him onto the mountain of Tayy. The ruler of Aylah gifted the Prophet ﷺ a white mule, clothed him with a mantle, and wrote for him concerning their sea territory. When he came to Wadi al-Qura, he said to the woman:

“How much did your garden produce?”

She said: “Ten awsuq, exactly as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ estimated.”

Then the Prophet ﷺ said:

“I am hurrying to Madinah, so whoever among you wants to hurry with me should do so.”

Then—after Ibn Bakkār said a word with this meaning—when he came near Madinah, he said:

“This is Tabah.”

When he saw Uhud, he said:

“This is a small mountain that loves us and we love it. Shall I tell you about the best homes of the Ansar?”

They said: “Yes.”

He said:

“The homes of Banu al-Najjar, then the homes of Banu ʿAbd al-Ashhal, then the homes of Banu Saʿidah or the homes of Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj — and there is good in every clan of the Ansar.”

Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (1481), and this is his wording, and Muslim (1392).

The phrase “Keep count” means: preserve the measured amount.

And in Muslim’s narration: “Keep count of it until we return to you, if Allah wills.”

٣٩٩١ — عن عبد الله بن عباس قال:

افتتح رسول اللّٰه ﷺ خيبر، واشترط أن له الأرض وكل صفراء وبيضاء. قال أهل خيبر: نحن أعلم بالأرض منكم، فأعطناها على أن لكم نصف الثمرة ولنا نصف. فزعم أنه أعطاهم على ذلك، فلما كان حين يُصرم النخل بعث إليهم عبد الله بن رواحة، فحرز عليهم النخل — وهو الذي يسمّيه أهل المدينة الخرص — فقال: في ذه كذا وكذا. قالوا: أكثرت علينا يا ابن رواحة. فقال: فأنا ألي حزر النخل وأعطيكم نصف الذي قلت. قالوا: هذا الحق، وبه تقوم السماء والأرض، قد رضينا أن نأخذه بالذي قلت.

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٤١٠)، وابن ماجه (١٨٢٠).

والخرص: من خَرَص يخرص، وهو تخمين ما على النخل من الرطب تمرًا، ليعرف مقدار ما يؤخذ منه وقت الجداد في العشر أو غيره.

3991 — ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbbas said:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ conquered Khaybar and stipulated that the land and all yellow and white wealth belonged to him. The people of Khaybar said: “We know the land better than you, so give it to us on the condition that you will have half the produce and we will have half.” When the time came to harvest the dates, he sent ʿAbdullah ibn Rawahah to estimate the palm trees — and this is what the people of Madinah call khars. He said: “This amount is such-and-such.” They said: “You have estimated too much against us, Ibn Rawahah.” He replied: “Then I will undertake the estimation of the palm trees and give you half of what I said.” They said: “This is the truth, and by it the heaven and the earth stand. We are satisfied to take it according to what you said.”

Hasan: narrated by Abu Dawud (3410) and Ibn Majah (1820).

Khars means estimating the amount of fresh dates on the trees as dried dates, so that the amount to be taken later at harvest time in zakat or otherwise may be known.
